sentence: This project studies how and why immune cells in blood vessels change to increase cardiovascular disease, using human subjects and mouse models of atherosclerosis.
This project studies the metabolic aspects of diseases, including heart failure, hepatocellular carcinoma, and undernutrition and iron metabolism.
This project uses gene editing to install common genetic alterations found in primary liver cancer into human liver cells and mice and studies their effects.
This project uses brain imaging and genetic approaches to study how the brain refines from adolescence to adulthood to support maturation of cognition.
This project shares a light-sheet microscopy system that examines cells, organs, and entire organisms at large scale.
This project combines enhanced T cells with an oncolytic virus to overcome barriers in treating solid tumors such as colorectal cancer.
This project studies the causes of age-related chronic inflammation and how it affects immunosuppression and cancer progression, using pre-clinical models and human samples.
This project studies the genetic architecture of the white matter network in the human brain and builds a tractography pipeline for severe mental illnesses.
This project uses deep-learning methods to design mini-proteins aimed at a cardiac channel for treating atrial fibrillation.
This project develops methods to measure the coronary microcirculation from clinical coronary angiography cine imaging data.
This project studies malaria transmission in Southeast Asia and looks for parasite antigens to improve point-of-care diagnosis.
This project develops human cochlear organoids, three-dimensional tissues that mimic the structure and function of native human cochleae.
This project studies the environmental and behavioral factors behind tick exposure and willingness to pay for tick control in rural and suburban populations.
This project studies the mechanisms that govern the biology of cancer, including how cancers initiate, progress, and evade therapies.
This project studies how two histone-modifying enzymes affect chondrocyte differentiation in craniofacial development and bone formation.
This project combines biophysical tools and molecular simulations to study the conformational dynamics of the HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein spike.
This project combines human and mouse data to determine how well mouse models of late-onset Alzheimer’s disease match human disease.
This project studies how the suction cup-like ventral disc of Giardia contracts so the parasite can attach to the host gut.
This project looks for molecular mechanisms and pharmacological agents that can protect bone after exposure to radiation.
This project studies how clonal expansions in the blood are linked to cardiovascular disease, including those without leukemogenic driver mutations.
